time.desc: The current government has officially stated that it will not force the platform to shut down on the statutory effective date and will transfer law enforcement responsibilities to the incoming new government.

The highest judicial body rejected the platform’s emergency relief request for an injunction, making it basically certain that the federal law of “forced divestment or removal” will take effect as scheduled.
As the ban was about to take effect, the platform briefly stopped serving domestic users and removed it from major app stores, causing actual availability disruptions.

The incoming government publicly promised to use administrative means to try to suspend the implementation of the ban and provide relevant service providers with an exemption signal. The platform subsequently resumed services to domestic users.
An ownership deal promoted by the new administration enters negotiations with a major technology company and outside investor group, with the parent company planning to retain a minority stake

Leader A publicly stated that it was negotiating with multiple parties for the acquisition of Platform X and would make a decision within 30 days, and named Entrepreneur E or Entrepreneur L E as potential buyers.

The new government passed an executive order to delay the implementation of the ban for several months to buy time for the transaction, but its legal effect and enforcement boundaries have caused controversy
Leaders signed an executive order to establish a government sovereign wealth fund and said the fund could be used to acquire the short video platform
Leader A Designates Vice President Vice President V to be responsible for facilitating the potential sale of Platform X
The short video platform has been re-listed in the main app stores first, but it is only available to old users who have already downloaded it, and new users cannot download it yet.
The judicial department issued written guarantees to major app store operators, and apps were restored to the shelves in domestic app stores, ending the phased download ban.

The head of the regulatory department wrote to the app store to make it clear that he will not be held accountable for hosting the distribution platform. The platform has been fully restored and the download ban has ended for more than three weeks.
A Northeast Asian country's regulatory agency confirmed that a chatbot company had shared user data with the platform's parent company and removed it from the platform the day before.
Private equity group investor BS is considering taking a stake in Platform X and may join the existing non-shareholder bidding camp. This team is regarded as the frontrunner for acquisitions.
Leader A first proposed that the November 26 ban cutoff may be further extended, and denied that the Platform X negotiations were directly related to the Country B tariff agreement

Leader A Government explores a trading option that would allow Company Y to retain Platform X core algorithms and license Country A on a lease basis for use by new entities to satisfy "foreign counterparty control" restrictions
The government once again extended the "sell or take it off the shelves" cutoff with an executive order before it expired, leaving a window for continued negotiations.

After Leader A announced the imposition of tariffs on Country B, Country B made it clear that it would not approve the Platform X transaction, and the sale plan that was originally close to completion was forced to be suspended.
The competent authority issues a disclaimer confirmation to the leading app store to continue hosting the app, allowing it to remain on the shelves and distributed during the extended period.

Multiple potential buyers have publicly expressed their interest in bidding for Platform X Country A business (including Figure 39, Figure 40, Figure 63, Internet celebrity 38, and the larger Company A M also submitted a bid at the last minute)
